- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope to reflect cooling.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.3), model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance or add 1-2% upward bias to capture momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5-7 days); apply a 2-5% upward bias to initial forecast values.  
- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., > 0.5 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to lag; delay peak forecast by 1-2 days and raise it 3-5% above historical mean.  
- If sentiment is volatile or erratic (e.g., alternating +/– > 0.5), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average or reduce amplitude of swings.
